newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares hit record on new Western wave.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares hit record on new Western wave.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rose in early trade on Monday on active demand from Western investors, said traders who saw the market continuing up in the next few days on what they called a new wave of interest in Russia.
The Russian Trading System opened at a record 391.26 after closing on Friday at a record 388.99.

Creditanstalt senior trader Andrei Galperin said Russia's inclusion in the Paris Club of creditor nations announced by U.S. President Bill Clinton during a Group of Seven leading nations summit in Colorado at the weekend had helped shares.
"Denver and the Paris Club gave the Russian equity market a new charge of popularity," said Galperin. "There's so much money on the market that it's difficult to see any kind of correction."
Senior United City Bank trader Samit Yakovlev said large orders were targetting a few highly-liquid stocks.
Oil company LUKoil LKOH.RTS jumped to $17.740 at 1018 GMT from $17.215 on Friday while Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS rose to $9.05 from an unofficial close on Friday of $8.56.
Norilsk rose rapidly on Friday after what traders termed a positive shareholders meeting.
The company said it would try to avoid issuing new shares to restructure its debt to the government and would not issue ADRs until it had achieved financial stability.
Yakovlev said Norilsk Nickel could rise to around $11 if long term investors bought shares in the company. Galperin said it would rise to around $9.50 on purely technical grounds.
National power company UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.3450 from $0.3314 while oil company Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS climbed to $1.08 from $1.02.
"There are some big clients here, so I see pretty good support for these shares," said Yakovlev, who saw the market rising through the middle of July.
"(Clients) are just afraid they won't be in time to buy and they are continuing to take the stock."
